messages:
Liam: FYI customer reported JSON-mode streaming responses getting cut off when their client does a quick reconnect. They pasted the partial payload and a curl trace.

Liam: customer snippet (truncated):
```json
{
  \"request_id\": \"req_9f1a\",
  \"response\": {
    \"items\": [
      {\"id\": \"itm_1\", \"value\": \"...\"},
      {\"id\": \"itm_2\", \"value\": \"partial...\"}
    ],
    \"summary\": \"Generat\"
```

Liam: curl they used: `curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -H \"Accept: application/json\" \"https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate?stream=true\"`

Maya: hitting :eyes: can you grab the full request_id and edge request id from customer? also what client/lib are they using (node fetch, golang http)?

Liam: sent request ids in DM: `req_9f1a` (customer) and edge `edge-rt-7a2b`. customer uses node-fetch v3 behind an internal proxy that aggressively reconnects on transient socket errors.

support-bot: Created ticket INF-3827 for this thread, assigned to eng-runtime.

Anna: 2 quick hypotheses: 1) upstream closed connection (runtime) and proxy returned partial chunk, 2) client reconnect logic reuses same TCP but closes stream mid-chunk leading to truncated final JSON chunk boundary. nginx/CF proxies sometimes drop the last chunk on FIN.

Jen: Repro checklist I'll try:
- curl with `-N` and `--no-buffer` to emulate streaming
- simulate reconnect: `nc -l 8080` -> proxy in front -> kill connection mid-stream
- try node fetch with `signal.abort()` after a small delay

Jen: example node repro (quick):
```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const controller = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 1200);
fetch(url, { headers, signal: controller.signal })
  .then(res => res.body.on('data', chunk => console.log(chunk.toString())))
  .catch(e => console.log('abort', e.message));
```

Maya: also paste the runtime logs around `edge-rt-7a2b` in infra. Look for: `upstream prematurely closed connection` or `broken pipe` or `client closed connection`. if we see `write() failed: Connection reset by peer` that points to client side.

Liam: copied relevant proxy log lines from customer (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-17T16:02:21Z] edge-rt-7a2b GET /v1/generate 200 0.867ms upstream: 10.0.2.34:8080 write() failed: Connection reset by peer
[2026-03-17T16:02:22Z] upstream closed prematurely while sending response to client
```

Anna: that `write() failed` + `upstream closed prematurely` makes me suspect our runtime closed the connection while the client was still reading, or the proxy observed a FIN from the client during the last chunk. we should check kernel-level logs around that req on the pod handling req_9f1a.

Maya: ask customer to try 2 quick workarounds and report which works: 1) set `stream=false` (non-streaming) 2) add a short polling retry when they get a parse error to request missing tail. also ask them to share their proxy type (nginx/istio/alb/cloudflare).

Liam: customer tried `stream=false` — works (complete JSON delivered). they also tried increasing client socket timeout and saw fewer truncations. they confirmed their proxy is `nginx` with `proxy_buffering on` and an aggressive `proxy_read_timeout 5s` in some internal hops.

Jen: moving forward:
- eng-runtime to add an extra `\"):__STREAM_END__\"` sentinel chunk as an optional compatibility flag for JSON-mode streaming that helps clients detect truncation.
- eng-infra to surface more detailed upstream-close reason in access logs for these cases.
- support to recommend temporary client-side retry-on-parse-error.

Anna: low-level next steps: grab the pod logs for the exact container and do `strace` on the process if we can repro locally to see whether `write()` returned EPIPE before our runtime finished sending closing braces.

Maya: assigned @Jen to run the node repro + nginx proxy config matrix and report results by EOD. I'll follow up with customer on suggested mitigations. :thumbsup:

Liam: thanks — attaching the short snippet I asked the customer to capture next time (curl --no-buffer -D - -o - ...). will update INF-3827 when we have repro steps.

support-bot: INF-3827 updated: labels: streaming, json-truncation, proxy; priority: high.
